title: Rehabilitation Program for People With Methamphetamine-Associated Cardiopulmonary Conditions
official: Feasibility of a Remote Collaborative Care-Facilitated Contingency Management-Exercise Rehabilitation Program for People With Methamphetamine-Associated Cardiopulmonary Conditions
summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of increasing control over stimulant use and physical health through incentivized rehabilitation (INSPIRE). INSPIRE is a 12-week remotely-delivered collaborative care intervention for rural patients with Methamphetamine-Associated Heart Failure (Me-HF) or Methamphetamine-Associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (Me-PAH) featuring smartphone-based contingency management incentivizing participation in remote synchronous rehabilitation.

interventions.name: Increasing control over stimulant use and physical health through incentivized rehabilitation

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Active methamphetamine use determined by positive urine drug testing within the past 3 months and/or self-reported current use
* Current diagnosis of chronic heart failure or pulmonary hypertension documented in the electronic health record
* Possession of a smartphone
* Able to participate in virtual exercise rehabilitation

Exclusion Criteria:

* Currently incarcerated
* Unable to interact with smartphone app and/or virtual health coaching sessions in English
* Unstable arrhythmia, defined as any known arrhythmia that is associated with hemodynamic effects like syncope, hypotension, or decompensated heart failure
* Decompensated chronic heart failure or pulmonary hypertension
* NYHA class IV symptoms
* Myocardial infarction within the past 3 months, percutaneous coronary intervention within the past 2 weeks, coronary artery bypass graft within the past 3 months, or implantable cardiac defibrillator/cardiac resynchronization therapy/pacemaker implantation within the last 6 weeks
* Unstable angina, uncontrolled hypertension, acute myocarditis/pericarditis, intracardiac thrombus
* Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis
